name: British Picturesque & Revival

description.short: The deliberate composition of irregular, historically allusive buildings for visual and emotional effect — the intellectual origin of nearly all Anglo-American suburban architecture.
description.long:
The picturesque begins as a theory of landscape and becomes a theory of building: that irregularity, variety, and historical association are legitimate architectural aims, and that a house may be composed like a painting. Once accepted, it licenses Gothic Revival, Scottish Baronial, Old English, Queen Anne, and eventually the entire vocabulary of the freestanding suburban house.

This family is where the classical assumption that a building should be symmetrical is abandoned as a general rule. Everything that follows in America — the Victorian villa, the Shingle Style, the ranch — depends on that permission having been granted.

defining_characteristics: Asymmetry and irregular massing as deliberate compositional choices
Historical association valued as a source of architectural meaning
Silhouette and skyline treated as primary design material
Texture and material variety used to animate surface
